This section;

>Each subverse has its own rules which are stated in respective subverse sidebars. If you ignore said rules, your account may be banned from submitting further content to the subverse or in some cases, globally.

Seems particularly open for abuse by moderators and leaves little to no redress for a community in the case of mod abuse.

Would it not be better to setup a site wide rule which prevents moderators from banning users/removing threads outside of spam and content which violates the laws of Switzerland?

In this way, mods would still be welcome to post guidelines on their respective sidebars with regards to how the community should be voting to keep the subverse "on topic", but mods would also be prohibited (via mandate) from censoring content on ideological grounds.

The issue with this medium is that unless there is an admin directive to stop mods from manipulating content under the guise of "subverse rules", the very same issue that occurred as a result of predatory mod behavior on reddit will be replicated here.

There was talk of a community based mechanism for removing unjust mods, but if mods are free to make whatever rules they please on their subverse they could easily create a rule which prohibits discussion of moderator actions.

To me, the above section of the FAQ poses a direct threat to the unique nature of this medium and I would implore you to change the language and implement a code of conduct for subverse moderators.

Yes, this rule needs some detailed review. Mods should have some control, especially of the smaller subs, but I don't want to come in one day and find that 40+ domains are banned in a sub with 3 million subscribers. Or that words are indiscriminately 'filtered' in another multimillion subscriber sub. Drawing the line is going to be difficult.
Stop trying to censor my freedom of expression by stopping me from enforcing my rules.
